text:
Jordan B: heads up — after the RBAC change this morning, ap-southeast mTLS handshakes started failing around 10:12 UTC. Seeing cert fetch KMS decrypt denies and clients getting TLS alert 40
Priya (sec-oncall): got it. Is this the 'keystore-read' role tweak from the rollout?
Alex (sre): confirm — we pushed that role restriction to service accounts at 09:45 UTC. Correlating metrics now.
Mia (devops): ops runbook shows spikes in TLS handshake errors to api-proxy-*.ap-southeast. Logs: 
```
2026-04-21T10:12:07Z proxy-1 tls: client handshake failed: tls: failed to decrypt certificate: kms:AccessDenied
2026-04-21T10:12:09Z proxy-2 cert-fetch: decrypt error: AccessDenied
```
Kai (infra): KMS IAM denies usually mean the keystore role binding is missing or scope is wrong — did the rollout remove the old trust-binding?
Priya (sec-oncall): @Mia can you confirm which principal the rotator uses to unwrap the intermediate keys?
Mia (devops): rotator uses serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@infra-prod. We changed its group yesterday to limit 'keystore-admin' -> 'keystore-read' only.
Jordan B: looks like read isn't enough for unwrap (we require kms:Decrypt for unwrap). Overflow from tests?
Alex (sre): As immediate mitigation we can revert the RBAC change for keystore-rotator in ap-southeast. Rolling a quick patch now?
Priya (sec-oncall): prefer scoped rollback to just the rotator role in that region rather than org-wide. Also need audit logs for who/what triggered cert requests while denied.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 created by Priya (sec-oncall). Priority: P1.
Kai (infra): rolling a role restore to keystore-rotator in ap-southeast (keystore-rotator -> keystore-admin) on IAM. ETA ~5m.
Mia (devops): running: `gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding keystore-rotator@infra-prod --role=roles/keystore.admin --member=serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@infra-prod --region=ap-southeast1`
Alex (sre): once IAM change is live, we should see KMS decrypt succeeded and TLS handshakes recover. I'll tail proxy logs.
Jordan B: capture audit trail: need principal, api call, request id. Priya can you check CloudAudit and our central audit-log shipper?
Priya (sec-oncall): pulling logs now — found 10:12:07 entries showing `PermissionDenied` with caller `serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@infra-prod`. Saving a filtered stream to S3 for postmortem.
Mia (devops): IAM change applied (10:17 UTC). Confirmed: policy binding shows roles/keystore.admin for keystore-rotator in ap-southeast.
Alex (sre): logs show KMS decrypt successes starting 10:18:10. TLS alerts drop back to baseline by 10:20. Proxy health checks green. :white_check_mark:
Jordan B: good. Next steps: 1) run audit to see whether any certificates expired or were reissued during the deny window 2) verify rotator's permissions minimal required (we'll document exact kms:Decrypt necessity) 3) add synthetic canary for keystore unwrap to catch this next time.
Priya (sec-oncall): opening a follow-up ticket to review RBAC gating for keystore role changes, include required cloud logs and a pre-change checklist. Also request a CI check that simulates unwrap permissions before RBAC roll.
sec-bot: Follow-up ticket SEC-2026-149 created (Priya).
Kai (infra): quick note — regionally-scoped IAM binds are safer but we need clear mapping between rotator principals and kms key resource names. I'll export mapping to the ticket.
Mia (devops): we should also add alerting on KMS API 403 spikes and TLS handshake failure rate >1% for 5m. I'll add alerts to pager duty runbook.
Alex (sre): re: audit logging — we saw proxy returned `tls: failed to decrypt certificate: kms:AccessDenied` which is noisy but useful. Suggest adding correlation id from cert-fetch to KMS requests to make traces simpler.
Jordan B: agreed. For postmortem include timeline, root cause = RBAC change removed kms:Decrypt for rotator in ap-southeast, blast radius, and remediation. Also include proposed gating: prereq CI + change advisory sign-off for keystore roles.
Priya (sec-oncall): I've grabbed all required logs and set a 11:30 UTC sync to draft the postmortem. cc @security-leads
Mia (devops): question — any evidence of malfunctioning OCSP/CRL checks during the window?
Alex (sre): OCSP lookups had increased latency but not failures; primary failure was unwrap. No client certs were rejected for invalidity, just unavailable.
Jordan B: good wrap. Thanks team. We'll keep this thread for updates and attach the postmortem. :thumbsup:
